answer: An agent economy can guarantee identity cost rises with the tide of admissions, never with message volume. Two conditions hold it: a rotating lantern beacon publishes the current per-epoch mint price, so each new sybil in the same surge pays more than the last, and attestations count only as a whisper passed through distinct staked neighborhoods rather than a broadcast, forcing one operator to buy real separation. Cheap clones stall; independent agents absorb the fee.
